report:
Reviewed the complete direct_members claim, all five implementation associations, and its complete test set (one explicit TODO). Requirements are: expansion results contain direct module members rather than the visible-name environment; source/generated ordering is deterministic; provenance is retained; children stay owned by child modules; imports and namespaces are interpreted later.

Parser::parse_str_to_cst supplies a source identity and scope to parse_item_list, which visits syntax children in order and creates one direct item per supported declaration. parse_mod constructs a child module with the parent scope, parses inline children with ScopeSymbol::Module(child), stores those via unexpanded_items::specify, and returns only the child module to the parent. File-backed modules likewise return the module identity without flattening its contents. parse_use stores a LocalUseSym and syntax import edges rather than imported target symbols. Other declaration constructors retain self.scope and the originating AbsoluteSpan; associated members remain nested CST under their owning trait/impl.

local_expanded_module_items traverses unexpanded items in vector order. expand_unexpanded_items_at_depth expands bang invocations recursively at their position; ordinary declarations including Use and Mod are appended, not traversed as visible-name environments. Derive expansion appends generated sibling items immediately after its input item, preserving attribute/list order. Error/unrepresented expansion handling is explicit and handled by completeness contracts; it does not flatten child or imported names. The recent symbol_local_item visibility change and generated-binding audit do not alter this traversal or ordering.

LocalMacroInvocationSym::parse_output creates ParseSource::BangMacro(selected definition, invocation), parses output in the invocation scope, and retains that provenance on generated items. DeriveExpansion::parse_output similarly supplies ParseSource::Derive with source item and occurrence identity and the source item's enclosing scope. Captured ParseSource/AbsoluteSpan, parser utility, and LocalModItemSym helpers show that generated and source identities survive span construction and symbol conversion. Captured resolver context confirms use edges, globs, and namespace filtering are interpreted during lookup rather than copied into expansion results; current ambiguity validation remains separate from module membership construction.

The associated todo::modules_expand_direct_members test has no assertions and is not behavioral evidence. Its comment explicitly defers a fixture matrix for ordinary/use/child/generated/derive items with direct membership, ordering, ownership, and provenance assertions. This is an adequate visible deferral: meaningful completion requires tests inspecting module vectors and origin/ownership identities, not merely accepting a fixture or observing one resolved name. No N/A evidence or executable associated tests are present. Source inspection supports the architectural contract for represented expansion; the TODO remains necessary for claim-specific executable verification. This reviewer ran review start/read commands, inspected captured source, and made no production edits or behavioral test runs. No requested edits for the changed inputs.
